Anyone counting this team out has not been watching them this season. Last night was a great example of a team that just doesn't give up. Honestly I would say that's more a testament as to how bad Boston is rather than how good we are. We are blowing away our projections this year, and I'm not complaining, but I think we're playing above our level and I'm astounded we've managed to keep the momentum going.

I think our 6-4 road stretch (could have been 8-2 honestly) showed that we're the real deal. It's hard to go into someone else's stadium and take the series from them. We did it twice and then split a series that we had chances to win/sweep. Now we're East Coast living for the rest of the season, let's go baby.
If there's anything that will help this team stay healthy, I think playing only in the eastern time zone the rest of the way will be it.

I agree that we're playing above our projections, but I think the projections relied heavily on A-Rod and Tex continuing to age. McCann has shown that last season was an outlier, not the beginning of a new trend. We didn't know what to expect from Didi, and he has more than earned his roster spot. The bullpen is tremendous, and the rotation is... underwhelming. Honestly, the only real question marks we have anymore come from the middle infield. Ryan hasn't had tons of playing time, but he has been better than we could have hoped offensively. Drew has a typical Drew average, but his flashes of power went a long way to get our offense going in the right direction early in the season.

Also, when I say the rotation isn't a question mark, I mean that we know it's going to be less than stellar.
